holidays.name: Ask a Stupid Question Day
holidays.description: It's a day to ask the question you've been too embarrassed to say out loud. Ask how airplanes stay up, why the sky is blue, or whether a hot dog counts as a sandwich. The day's motto is that the only dumb question is the one you never asked.
holidays.origin: The observance dates to the early 1980s. It was created to encourage students to speak up in class without fear of judgment. Teachers and librarians have since embraced it as a way to encourage curiosity.
holidays.funFact: Ask a Stupid Question Day was established in 1982. Over the years it has been listed on different dates, including the last school day of September, but September 28 is the date most calendars now use.

holidays.name: Fish Amnesty Day
holidays.description: A day to stop and think about the fish in our lives, from the ones in the ocean to the ones on our plates. People mark it by learning about how smart and social fish are. Some also swap seafood for plant-based meals for the day.
holidays.origin: PETA designated September 28 as Fish Amnesty Day. The goal is to raise awareness that fish are sentient beings that feel pain and deserve compassion.
holidays.funFact: Fish are more clever than their reputation suggests. Many species can recognize individual faces, use tools, and build complex social relationships. So the old idea of a three-second goldfish memory is a myth.
